High-field-side (inboard) equatorial midplane - the inner-midplane counterpart of outboard_midplane. The inner-midplane reference is the inboard intersection of the horizontal plane through the magnetic axis (or the DD midplane_identifier) with the plasma boundary / first wall. DD: e.g. equilibrium/time_slice/profiles_1d/r_inboard (inboard major radius of the flux surface at the midplane).

A nuclide of an element distinguished by its neutron number.
An electrode diagnostic that infers local plasma properties from its current-voltage response.
The location at which a Langmuir probe tip samples the local plasma, embedded or reciprocating. Distinct from langmuir_probe, the probe itself as an entity.
The outermost magnetic flux surface whose field lines close toroidally, bounding the confined-plasma region.
The spatial location identified as the launching position in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.

Plasma-facing limiter. As a measurement locus, 'at_limiter' denotes the scrape-off-layer plasma immediately adjacent to the limiter surface; the DD provides only the limiter surface geometry (wall/description_2d/limiter) and the precise plasma evaluation point is not yet standardised (IMAS_3226). For the separatrix-limiter tangency CONTACT point use active_limiter_point; for a quantity distributed OVER the limiter surface (e.g. a peak power density) use the 'along' relation (along_limiter).
The limiter tile treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The directed observation path from a diagnostic aperture or detector through the observed domain.
The lower hybrid antenna treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The lower hybrid antenna row treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged.
A diagnostic sensor used to measure a component of the local magnetic field.
The mass spectrometer treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The mass spectrometer channel treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The position in the cylindrical frame at which a diagnostic channel samples, used for the coordinates of that position where the coordinate serves many instrument families.
A reference plane through the tokamak on which the vertical coordinate is zero in the adopted coordinate system.
The surface where the absolute value of the safety factor is minimum.
The mse treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.

A location selected by a specified normalized poloidal-magnetic-flux value.
A component that redirects, filters, focuses, disperses, or otherwise transforms electromagnetic radiation.

Low-field-side (outboard) equatorial midplane. The outer-midplane reference follows the DD midplane_identifier (default option 'dr_dz_zero_sep': the outboard separatrix point where dr/dz = 0). For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix.

Intersection of the separatrix with the outboard (low-field-side) midplane - the outboard separatrix point where dr/dz = 0 (the local major-radius maximum of the separatrix). This is where a separatrix POINT value is evaluated. DD: equilibrium/time_slice/boundary_separatrix/dr_dz_zero_point; outer-midplane reference per the midplane_identifier.
The spatial location identified as the outer in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The spatial location identified as the outlet in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The passive loop treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
A discrete geometry element of a passive conducting loop.
The passive structure treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.

H-mode edge transport-barrier (pedestal) region. Ambiguous as a single point: for a profile VALUE use pedestal_top; for a maximum-gradient or fit POSITION use pedestal_maximum. Prefer the more specific token over this bare one. DD: summary/local/pedestal, summary/pedestal_fits/*.

Location of the maximum pedestal gradient (the steep mid-pedestal), i.e. the peak-gradient / fit position of the edge barrier. Distinct from the pedestal top. DD: summary/pedestal_fits/*/d_dpsi_norm_max_position, summary/local/pedestal/position/psi.
The edge transport-barrier region characterized by steep plasma-profile gradients.
Top of the H-mode edge pedestal (the barrier's inner shoulder), where 'the pedestal value' of a profile is conventionally reported. DD: summary/pedestal_fits/* pedestal-top fit outputs.
The spatial location identified as the pedestal top high field side in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The spatial location identified as the pedestal top low field side in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.

A solid fragment produced by shattering an injected pellet.
The pellet injector treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.

An optical element whose relevant function is reflection from a defined surface.
A toroidal winding used to measure the electric current enclosed by its path.
The saddle loop treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The spatial location identified as the sawtooth inversion radius in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The spatial location identified as the sawtooth mixing radius in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The plasma region outside the last closed flux surface whose open field lines intersect material surfaces.

The spatial location identified as the spectral line in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
A diagnostic system that resolves detected radiation or particles by energy, wavelength, frequency, or mass-to-charge ratio.
The spectrometer channel treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The strain gauge treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The strain gauge sensor treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The point where a divertor separatrix branch intersects a plasma-facing target.
The spatial location identified as the tearing mode center in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.

The scattering volume assigned to one Thomson-scattering channel.

The spatial region enclosed by the vacuum-vessel boundary.
The visible camera treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The spatial location identified as the wall in the relevant plasma, diagnostic, or plant context.
The wall material treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.
The wave beam treated as a distinct physical, plant, or diagnostic object in a standard name.

NAMES.name: capacitance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Effective capacitance of an impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna, relating stored charge to the RF voltage used for circuit
tuning.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative lumped capacitance associated with an
impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module. It
represents the element's ability to store electric charge and participate in
tuning the radio-frequency transmission circuit.

For an ideal lumped capacitive element, the capacitance is defined by

$$
C = \frac{Q}{V}
$$

where $C$ is the capacitance, $Q$ is the charge stored on the element, and
$V$ is the electric potential difference across the element.

The quantity applies to the specified matching element of the antenna and
does not represent the capacitance of an unrelated circuit component or the
entire transmission system. It is a circuit parameter rather than a power,
current, or operating-frequency quantity.

Together with the [resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), it characterizes
the antenna's effective RF impedance; the [frequency of an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna](name:frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) identifies
the RF operating frequency at which the matching condition is evaluated.

NAMES.name: forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Forward RF power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the incident power
traveling from the generator toward the antenna before reflection and
coupling to the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the forward-traveling
RF power at a defined reference plane on the feed line, directed from the
generator toward the antenna. It is the incident power arriving at the
antenna before reflection at the antenna–plasma interface and before power
is coupled into the plasma.

The quantity applies to one antenna or antenna module at its feed-line
reference plane and includes only the forward-traveling component; it is not
summed over an antenna system. It excludes backward-traveling [reflected
power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and power
already coupled into the plasma.

At a common reference plane, forward and reflected power determine the net
[launched power]: the launched component is the forward power less the
reflected power when intervening feed-line losses are excluded.

NAMES.name: frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Radio-frequency drive frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna,
averaged over its modules. This non-negative scalar sets the ion-cyclotron
resonance layer locations and the ion species and harmonics accessible for
wave absorption.
NAMES.long:
Radio-frequency drive frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the
non-negative cycle frequency of the electromagnetic drive applied to the
antenna. It is an antenna-level setting that enters the ion-cyclotron
resonance condition for wave absorption by ions in the plasma.

For an ion species resonating at harmonic $n$, the defining resonance
relation is:

$$
2\pi f = n\Omega_{ci} = n\frac{Z_i e B}{m_i}
$$

where $f$ is this radio-frequency drive frequency, $n$ is the positive
integer ion-cyclotron harmonic number, $i$ labels the resonant ion species,
$\Omega_{ci}$ is the ion cyclotron angular frequency of species $i$, $Z_i$
is the charge number of species $i$, $e$ is the elementary charge, $B$ is
the magnetic-field magnitude at the resonant location, and $m_i$ is the mass
of species $i$.

This quantity applies to a complete ion-cyclotron heating antenna, not to a
single antenna module; if module frequencies differ, its aggregation
convention is the arithmetic mean over the modules. It is the ordinary cycle
frequency $f$, not the angular frequency $2\pi f$, and it is distinct from
the spatially varying local ion cyclotron frequency in the plasma.

The frequency, together with the selected ion species, harmonic number, and
magnetic-field magnitude, determines which resonance layers are accessible,
but it does not by itself identify a unique absorption channel when several
species or harmonics satisfy the resonance relation. It is separate from
total_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna, from the RF-circuit quantity
[resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna),
and from voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna; the analogous
electron-cyclotron quantity is
[frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_heating_antenna](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam).

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the net RF power entering the
vacuum vessel after reflection at the antenna input reference plane.
NAMES.long:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative net RF power
propagating from the antenna input reference plane into the vacuum vessel
toward the plasma. It is one per-antenna component of the wave-power budget
represented by [power of a lower-hybrid antenna].

The net launched power is defined by:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident RF power arriving at the antenna
input reference plane and $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the RF power returning
toward the transmission line. The quantity applies to one lower-hybrid
antenna and is not an aggregate over multiple antennas.

Launched power is distinct from [forward power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), which includes power
subsequently reflected, and from [reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It denotes power
entering the vacuum vessel, not generator output or power subsequently
absorbed by the plasma. Mode-resolved representations, including [per
toroidal mode launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna], resolve this same
per-antenna quantity by wave-number interval.

NAMES.name: net_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Net ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power launched into the vacuum vessel by a
specified heating launcher before absorption by plasma particles.
NAMES.long:
Net ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power is the power delivered through a
specified ion-cyclotron heating antenna into the vacuum vessel toward the
plasma. It is a launcher-boundary quantity, not the power ultimately
absorbed by plasma particles.

The defining net-power relation is:

$$
P_{\rm launched}=P_{\rm forward}-P_{\rm reflected}
$$

where $P_{\rm launched}$ is the net power launched toward the plasma,
$P_{\rm forward}$ is the incident radio-frequency power traveling toward the
antenna as described by [forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and $P_{\rm
reflected}$ is the radio-frequency power returned from the antenna toward
the source as described by [reflected power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna).

The quantity applies to one specified ion-cyclotron heating launcher and
represents its launcher-associated power. It has no species, charge-state,
or volumetric deposition resolution and is not an all-antenna aggregate.

Reflected power is excluded from the launched result, as are power losses
upstream of the antenna boundary and power subsequently absorbed by plasma
particles. The launcher-resolved quantity is the per-launcher counterpart of
[power due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating); summing corresponding
launcher values gives [total power due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating), while [launched
power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) expresses the
same boundary power with the antenna as the explicit object locus.

NAMES.name: pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Pressure associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module,
representing mechanical normal loading or contained-gas pressure at hardware
components.
NAMES.long:
Pressure associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module represents
the compressive normal stress or contained-gas pressure acting at its
hardware components.

At a surface, pressure is defined as the normal force distributed over the
loaded area:

$$
p = \frac{F_n}{A}
$$

where $p$ is pressure, $F_n$ is the force normal to the surface, and $A$ is
the area over which that force acts. For contained gas, the same scalar
represents the isotropic normal stress exerted by the gas.

The scope is the antenna module and its associated hardware components,
including local mechanical or gas-pressure conditions at individual sensing
locations. The quantity is not a plasma pressure, a pressure amplitude, a
pressure variation, or an aggregate sum or average over the module.

Pressure is a mechanical or fluid-state property and is independent of
electrical properties such as the antenna's
[resistance](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [strap
current].

NAMES.name: radial_outline_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of each point on an antenna-strap outline in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity gives the major-radius coordinate of a point on the geometric
outline of an antenna strap. It identifies the point's perpendicular
distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity is pointwise and unaggregated over the antenna-strap outline:
each value applies to one outline point. It does not represent the strap's
reference-point coordinate, center coordinate, radial extent, or
outer-radius bound.

The complementary [toroidal angle of the antenna
strap](name:toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap) specifies the angular location
of the same outline point. The [radial coordinate of the antenna
strap](name:radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap) instead locates a specified
strap geometry reference point and is therefore not interchangeable with
this outline coordinate.

NAMES.name: reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase angle of a reflected radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
antenna element in an ion-cyclotron heating launcher, measured relative to
the forward power-wave phasor of that same element.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the relative phase of a complex reflected radio-frequency
power-wave phasor at a selected antenna strap or module with respect to the
complex forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor of the same strap or
module. It specifies the element-local reflection phase of an ion-cyclotron
heating launcher rather than an absolute phase or an inter-element phase.

For element $i$, the reflected phase is defined by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \arg\!\left(b_i^{\mathrm{ref}} (a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i}$ is this reflected phase, $b_i^{\mathrm{ref}}$
is the complex reflected power-wave phasor at element $i$,
$a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the complex forward power-wave phasor at the same
element, $(a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*$ is its complex conjugate, and $\arg$
extracts the phase angle. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The scope is a single selected launcher strap or module and the pair of
forward and reflected traveling power waves at the same element reference
plane. The forward wave propagates toward the antenna element, and the
reflected wave propagates away from the antenna element toward the feeding
network. The first launcher element is not the phase reference for this
quantity, and the quantity is not averaged or summed over launcher elements.

This quantity is a reflected-wave member of the broader [phase of the
ion-cyclotron heating antenna] family. It is distinct from the [wave phase
of the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which describes
inter-element phasing, and together with the [reflected power of the
ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) it specifies
the phase-and-magnitude state of the reflected power wave without including
the magnitude itself.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the reflected-wave phasor at the selected
element leads the forward-wave phasor at the same element in phase under the
adopted temporal phasor convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the reflected power with respect to the forward power of this module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Reflected power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the
backward-traveling radio-frequency power returned from one antenna toward
the transmission-line source rather than coupled into the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Reflected power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the
backward-traveling radio-frequency wave power at a defined reference plane
on the feed line, directed away from the antenna toward the source. It is
the returned component of the antenna-associated power and represents
incident power rejected by antenna-plasma coupling.

At a common reference plane, the reflected and forward traveling-wave powers
are related by

$$
P_{\mathrm{ref}} = |\Gamma|^2 P_{\mathrm{fwd}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reflected power, $\Gamma$ is the complex
wave reflection coefficient, and $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) traveling toward
the antenna.

This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna and represents
the aggregate returned power associated with that antenna at the defined
reference plane. When an antenna contains multiple modules, it is distinct
from reflected power assigned to an individual module; it also excludes
forward power, power coupled into the plasma, and source power not present
at the reference plane.

It complements [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) as the opposite
traveling-wave component at the feed-line reference plane. The [launched
power] is power delivered from the antenna into the plasma, so it is
physically distinct from returned reflected power; the two quantities must
not be identified or substituted for one another.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular coordinate of each antenna-strap outline point around the
machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal angle is the azimuthal coordinate assigned to each point on the
geometric outline of an antenna strap. It identifies the point’s
circumferential location in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to individual strap-outline points and is not a mean,
sum, nominal center coordinate, or mechanical orientation angle. No
aggregation over the outline is implied; each point retains its own $\phi$
value.

Together with the other coordinates of the outline, this angle locates the
strap geometry. It is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the antenna
strap](name:radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap), which locates a strap
reference point, while [vertical outline of the antenna
strap](name:vertical_outline_of_antenna_strap) provides the corresponding
signed vertical coordinate for outline points. The same angular-coordinate
concept is used for a different object by [toroidal angle of a coil
conductor element](name:toroidal_angle_of_coil_conductor_element).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the angular displacement from the chosen
$\phi=0$ reference is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Strap outline

NAMES.name: toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Full toroidal width of the rectangular cross-section of an ICRH antenna
strap conductor element, measured along the toroidal direction in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Full toroidal width of the rectangular cross-section of an ICRH antenna
strap conductor element, measured along the toroidal direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the edge-to-edge
extent between the two toroidally separated sides of the strap conductor.

For a strap represented at a characteristic major radius, the toroidal width
is related to the angular separation of the two toroidal edges by:

$$
w_\phi = R_\mathrm{strap}\,\Delta\phi
$$

where $w_\phi$ is the toroidal width, $R_\mathrm{strap}$ is the
representative major radius of the strap, and $\Delta\phi$ is the smaller
non-wrapping angular separation between the two toroidal edges.

This is a full width, not a half-width or a signed coordinate difference. It
is distinct from the poloidal extent
[height_of_antenna_strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap) and from the
local-normal extent
[thickness_of_antenna_strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap) of the same
strap conductor.

NAMES.name: total_external_heating_power
NAMES.short:
Total non-inductive power coupled from external neutral-beam and
radio-frequency heating systems to the plasma, summed over auxiliary sources
and excluding Ohmic heating.
NAMES.long:
Total external heating power is the aggregate non-inductive power coupled to
the plasma by auxiliary heating systems. It includes neutral-beam injection
and electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron, and lower-hybrid systems, while
excluding power associated with Ohmic induction.

The defining aggregate relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ext}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}} P_s
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the total external heating power,
$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the set of included auxiliary heating
systems, and $P_s$ is the power coupled to the plasma by auxiliary source
$s$.

The quantity applies to the whole plasma and is summed over all included
auxiliary sources rather than resolved by source, species, or spatial
region. It represents external power input that may contribute to both
plasma heating and non-inductive current drive; it is distinct from Ohmic
heating and from generator power that is not coupled to the plasma.
Source-specific contributions include [total power due to electron-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating), [total power
due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating), and power absorbed
from a [neutral-beam injector], whose aggregate forms contribute to the sum.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total additional external power (NBI+EC+IC+LH, without ohmic) coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Total ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power launched into the vacuum vessel by
the complete heating-antenna system, summed over all antennas.
NAMES.long:
Total ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power is the aggregate power launched
into the vacuum vessel by the complete ion-cyclotron heating-antenna system.
It represents the net launcher-array power directed toward the plasma,
rather than power ultimately absorbed by plasma particles.

The system total is defined by summing the launched power from each antenna:

$$
P_{\rm total}=\sum_{i=1}^{N_{\rm ant}} P_i
$$

where $P_{\rm total}$ is the total ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power
launched by the system, $N_{\rm ant}$ is the number of contributing
ion-cyclotron heating antennas, $i$ is an antenna index, and $P_i$ is the
net power launched by antenna $i$, corresponding to the antenna-resolved
[ion-cyclotron heating power].

The quantity applies to the complete heating system and is aggregated over
all ion-cyclotron heating antennas. It has no individual-antenna, species,
charge-state, or volumetric deposition resolution. Reflected power and
losses upstream of the vacuum-vessel launch boundary are excluded, and the
quantity does not represent the portion subsequently absorbed by plasma
particles.

This system-level total is the aggregate counterpart of [launched power due
to ion-cyclotron heating](name:launched_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating),
while [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) represents
the corresponding launcher-oriented power for an individual antenna.

NAMES.short:
Signed vertical coordinate of each contour point defining an ion-cyclotron

NAMES.long:
The vertical outline coordinate is the signed height of one contour point on
the geometric boundary of an ion-cyclotron antenna strap, expressed in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It describes boundary
geometry rather than a field or thermodynamic quantity.

The quantity applies pointwise to the strap outline: each value belongs to
one boundary contour point. Values are not summed, averaged, or integrated
over the outline, and the quantity does not represent the strap's
geometric-center location.

The geometric-center location is represented separately by the [vertical
coordinate of the antenna strap](name:vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap).
Collectively, the coordinates of corresponding outline points define the
strap boundary geometry.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Strap outline

NAMES.name: voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency voltage waveform on a single
transmission-line feed of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency electrical
potential difference on one transmission-line feed belonging to an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.

For the feed voltage waveform $v(t)$, its amplitude is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t |v(t)|
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the voltage amplitude, $v(t)$ is the
instantaneous feed voltage, and $t$ is time. The absolute value removes
instantaneous polarity, while the maximum selects the peak magnitude of the
waveform.

The quantity applies to one feed of one antenna module and is not a sum over
feeds, antenna modules, or the complete heating system. It excludes the
instantaneous signed voltage and its phase; it also does not represent
forward or launched radio-frequency power. It is the amplitude
transformation of the corresponding [ion-cyclotron-heating antenna
voltage](name:voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), retaining the feed
voltage's peak level while discarding its instantaneous sign and phase.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

NAMES.name: wave_current_amplitude_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current at a specified position along
an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current on an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap at a specified position. It
characterizes the local electromagnetic excitation of a strap fed through a
single transmission line.

The amplitude $I_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is defined from the local RF current
waveform $i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ by

$$
I_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t \left|i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)\right|
$$

where $i_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ is the instantaneous radio-frequency current at
the specified strap position and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies locally along the antenna strap and represents the RF
wave-current amplitude, not a current summed over the antenna system or over
multiple straps. It is a non-negative magnitude and is distinct from the
signed instantaneous current and from an RMS current measure.

It is the amplitude transformation of the [wave current of an antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap): the parent denotes the
oscillating current, whereas this quantity retains its peak magnitude at the
specified position.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of current measurements

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Phase angle of the radio-frequency current phasor carried by one
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap, defined relative to a specified RF
phase reference.
NAMES.long:
Wave phase of an antenna strap is the phase angle of the oscillatory
radio-frequency current phasor carried by that strap. It describes the
strap-level excitation phase used in the antenna's toroidal phasing
configuration.

The complex strap-current phasor may be represented as

$$
I_s = |I_s|e^{i\phi_s}
$$

where $I_s$ is the complex radio-frequency current phasor, $|I_s|$ is its
current amplitude, and $\phi_s$ is the wave phase represented by this
quantity. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ relative to a specified RF
reference phase.

This quantity applies to one antenna strap and is not summed or averaged
over multiple straps. It refers to the phase of the strap current, not the
phase of a forward power-wave phasor, which is represented by [forward wave
phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), or the
phase associated with a complete antenna element.

The associated [wave current of antenna strap] provides the phasor whose
phase is specified, while [wave current of antenna strap amplitude]
determines its magnitude rather than its phase. Relative phases between
straps determine the toroidal phasing of the antenna excitation and
therefore influence the launched wave excitation spectrum. The
phase-reference plane and any phase-unwrapping convention must be specified
separately when comparing values.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the strap current
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase angle of a radio-frequency phasor at an antenna element in an
ion-cyclotron heating launcher, measured relative to the first element for
inter-element phasing.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the relative phase of a complex radio-frequency phasor at a
selected antenna strap or module feed with respect to the first reference
element. It specifies inter-element phasing of an ion-cyclotron heating
launcher rather than an absolute phase.

For selected element $i$, the relative phase is defined by

$$
\Delta\phi_i = \arg\left(A_i A_1^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\Delta\phi_i$ is the relative phase of element $i$, $A_i$ is its
complex radio-frequency voltage or wave phasor, $A_1$ is the phasor of the
first reference element, $A_1^*$ is the complex conjugate of that reference
phasor, and $\arg$ extracts the phase angle. The reference element has zero
relative phase, and the result is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The quantity applies independently to one selected antenna element or module
feed and is not summed or averaged over modules. It describes the
radio-frequency signal associated with the antenna feed, not a phase
belonging to a plasma population or integrated over a plasma region. It
excludes absolute phase, amplitude, power, and reflection coefficient,
although the phase may characterize a complex feed voltage or traveling-wave
quantity.

The family parent [phase of the ion-cyclotron heating antenna] provides the
common relative-phase meaning. Propagation-specific instances retain this
definition while selecting the wave direction, as in the [forward wave phase
of the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and the
[reflected phase of the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected element's radio-frequency phasor
leads the first reference element in phase under the adopted temporal phasor
convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

NAMES.name: forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase of the forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module, referenced to the first module for
inter-module toroidal phasing.
NAMES.long:
The forward-wave phase is the relative phase angle of the complex
radio-frequency power-wave phasor associated with one ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna module. It describes inter-module phasing rather than an absolute
phase.

For selected module $i$, the relative forward-wave phase is defined by

$$
\theta_i^{+} = \arg\left(\tilde{a}_i^{+}\right) - \arg\left(\tilde{a}_1^{+}\right)
$$

where $\theta_i^{+}$ is the relative forward-wave phase, $i$ identifies the
selected antenna module, module $1$ is the first reference module,
$\tilde{a}_i^{+}$ is the complex phasor of the forward radio-frequency power
wave associated with module $i$, and $\arg$ returns a phasor's phase angle.

The quantity applies only to the forward wave at an antenna module and is
defined relative to the first module; no absolute phase relative to a
generator or external reference is implied. It concerns the electromagnetic
power-wave phasor, not a plasma-particle quantity or a spatially distributed
plasma field.

This is the forward-wave specialization of the relative antenna phasor phase
defined by [wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna). It is distinct
from the relative phase of the reflected wave, [reflected phase of an
ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and from
the phase of the RF current carried by an antenna strap, [wave phase of an
antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected module's forward-wave phasor
leads the first reference module in phase.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the forward power with respect to the first module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of the electron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for free electrons at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the electron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the electron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local electron number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_e = \frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $N_e$ is the number of free electrons in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the free-electron population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and counts each free electron once, without
charge-state weighting. Electrons bound in atoms or molecules, ions, and
other neutral particles are excluded.

Unlike
[total_ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target),
which sums positive-ion densities over ion species and charge states, this
quantity describes the electron population and is not an ionic density or a
charge density.

sources.parent_definition: Description of SOL according to the two point model, the downstream point being on this target, for various time slices

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron density

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per
particle of the electron population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath, distinct from the target material temperature.
NAMES.long:
Electron temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per
particle of the electron population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It is a plasma boundary quantity for electrons at
the downstream end of the scrape-off layer, not a thermodynamic property of
the solid target material.

For the electron population, the target temperature is the one-third trace
of the kinetic thermal-energy moment at the sheath edge:

$$
T_{e,t} = \frac{m_e}{3 n_{e,t}} \int |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{e,t}|^2 f_{e,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{e,t}$ is the electron temperature at the divertor target, $m_e$ is
the electron mass, $n_{e,t}$ is the free-electron number density at the
sheath edge, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{e,t}$ is the
mean electron flow velocity at the sheath edge, $f_{e,t}(\mathbf{v})$ is the
electron velocity distribution there, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element.

This quantity applies exclusively to the free-electron population at a
specified divertor target and represents a density-weighted per-particle
thermal energy scale rather than an extensive sum. It excludes ion,
neutral-particle, and solid-target temperatures, and it is not an average
over multiple plasma populations.

It is the electron-specific component of [temperature at the divertor
target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target). The electron density at the
same locus, [electron density at divertor
target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), supplies the local
population density appearing in the defining moment but is a distinct
quantity.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_maximum_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Peak local energy-deposition rate per unit area on one divertor target
surface, combining incident plasma-particle and radiative energy-carrying
channels.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the greatest local energy-deposition flux on the
plasma-facing surface of one divertor target. It represents the peak heat
load per unit area from the combined incident particle and radiative
energy-carrying channels.

The peak is defined from the local [energy flux at a divertor
target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target) by

$$
q_{E,\mathrm{peak}} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S_t} q_E(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $q_{E,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the peak energy flux, $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ is
the local deposited energy flux at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $S_t$
is the plasma-facing surface of one divertor target.

The maximum is taken over surface locations on a single divertor target.
This quantity is not an integral over the target or divertor assembly, and
it does not select only the inner or outer target; those distinctions are
separate physical or positional scopes. It includes the combined local
contribution of the applicable particle and radiative channels.

The parent quantity [energy flux at a divertor
target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target) describes the local field from
which this peak is obtained, whereas [power at a divertor
target](name:power_at_divertor_target) is an integrated deposition rate
rather than a per-area maximum.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive
particle count per physical volume for the electron population evaluated on
the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting
closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local electron number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the
electron distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the
last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron
velocity, $f_e$ is the electron phase-space distribution function, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to electrons and is not an ion or
neutral-particle density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging
over the boundary surface or over a volume; because electrons are not
resolved here into atomic ionization states, no charge-state aggregation is
applied.

It is the electron-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary instead represents
the average of electron density over the same last closed magnetic flux
surface, rather than the local value.

sources.parent_definition: Electron density

NAMES.name: total_power_at_separatrix
NAMES.short:
Net energy power leaving the confined plasma through the last closed
magnetic flux surface and entering the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Separatrix power is the net global energy loss from the confined plasma into
the scrape-off layer across the last closed magnetic flux surface. It
represents the aggregate power crossing the entire separatrix rather than a
local surface value.

The defining boundary integral is

$$
P_{\rm sep} = \oint_{S_{\rm sep}} \mathbf{S}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix power, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the last
closed magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{S}_E$ is the net plasma-energy flux
density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the confined
plasma toward the scrape-off layer, and $dA$ is an element of separatrix
area.

This is a total, net quantity integrated over the complete separatrix. It
applies to the confined plasma as a whole, with no selection of species,
reaction channel, or individual transport mechanism; outward energy transfer
is the plasma loss represented by the quantity. It is not a pointwise
energy-flux density or a power associated with a single surface location.

The boundary total is distinct from [radiated power over the core
region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), which describes
electromagnetic power emitted within the core and is not necessarily equal
to power crossing the separatrix. It is also distinct from [power due to
conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), which describes
conduction-mediated power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces downstream of
the separatrix.

sources.parent_definition: Power through separatrix

NAMES.name: frequency_of_wave_diagnostic_channel
NAMES.short:
Temporal frequency associated with a wave-diagnostic channel, defining the
oscillation or probing frequency used to establish its plasma interaction.
NAMES.long:
The wave-diagnostic-channel frequency is the temporal rate of oscillation of
the electromagnetic wave associated with a channel. It specifies the
frequency at which the channel interacts with or samples the plasma.

The relation between temporal frequency $f$ and angular frequency $\omega$
is

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is the temporal frequency, $\omega$ is the angular frequency of
the wave, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

This quantity applies to one wave-diagnostic channel and is not a sum or
average over channels, frequency values, or wave power. For a
frequency-swept probing channel, each selected frequency defines the probing
state used to determine the corresponding plasma response or cutoff
location; for a resonance channel, it identifies the wave frequency
associated with the probed resonance.

The channel-owned quantity is distinct from the broader [wave
frequency](name:wave_frequency) concept and from the beam-owned [frequency
of an electron-cyclotron beam](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam).
It describes frequency, not the duration of a sweep or the electromagnetic
energy-transfer rate represented by [wave power](name:wave_power).

NAMES.name: initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
NAMES.short:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the electric-field
polarization ellipse of a polarimeter probing beam in its incident state,
before plasma entry. It gives only the ellipticity component of the initial
polarization vector, not the ellipse orientation.
NAMES.long:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the electric-field
polarization ellipse of a polarimeter probing beam in its incident state,
before plasma entry, is the initial polarization ellipticity of that beam.
It is the ellipticity component of the beam's initial polarization vector
and specifies the shape and handedness of the incident polarization ellipse,
not its orientation.

For an incident electric-field polarization ellipse with major semiaxis
amplitude $a_0$ and minor semiaxis amplitude $b_0$, the initial ellipticity
$\epsilon_0$ is defined by:

$$
\epsilon_0 = \sigma_0 \frac{b_0}{a_0}
$$

where $\epsilon_0$ is the initial polarization ellipticity, $a_0$ is the
major semiaxis amplitude, $b_0$ is the minor semiaxis amplitude with $0 \le
b_0 \le a_0$, and $\sigma_0$ is the handedness sign of the incident
polarization state.

This quantity applies to a single polarimeter probing beam along a specified
line of sight in its pre-plasma state. It is not averaged or summed over
multiple lines of sight, and it does not describe the full polarization
vector, beam intensity, wavelength, path geometry, path-integrated
ellipticity, or any post-plasma polarization state.

It provides the reference value for Cotton-Mouton ellipticity changes
induced during traversal of magnetized plasma. It is the incident-state
counterpart of [polarization ellipticity of a polarimeter
beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam), which denotes the
polarization ellipticity after plasma traversal; it is distinct from the
[Faraday angle](name:faraday_angle), which describes rotation of the
polarization-ellipse orientation rather than the semiaxis ratio.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when, in the right-handed beam-local basis
$(\hat{e}_1, \hat{e}_2, \hat{k})$ with $\hat{k}$ along beam propagation,
$\hat{e}_1$ along the major semiaxis, and $\hat{e}_2 = \hat{k} \times
\hat{e}_1$, the electric-field vector rotates from $+\hat{e}_1$ toward
$+\hat{e}_2$ as time increases.

NAMES.name: length_variation_of_interferometer_beam
NAMES.short:
Signed plasma-induced change in the effective optical path accumulated along
an interferometer beam relative to its corresponding no-plasma reference
path.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed plasma-induced change in effective optical path
length accumulated along an electromagnetic propagation path represented by
an interferometer beam. It describes an optical delay or advance caused by
the plasma, rather than the unperturbed geometric path length.

The variation is defined as

$$
\Delta L = L_{\mathrm{plasma}} - L_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\Delta L$ is the optical path-length variation, $L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$
is the effective optical path along the beam in the presence of plasma, and
$L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the corresponding effective path without plasma.

This quantity applies to the net change accumulated along the interferometer
beam's complete line of sight. It is a path-integrated optical quantity, not
a local path-length density, an unperturbed geometric length, or a separate
phase-calibration coefficient. As the variation of [length of an
interferometer beam](name:length_of_interferometer_beam), it expresses the
plasma-induced departure from the reference path. The associated phase shift
provides the optical information used to derive [line-integrated electron
number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the plasma-affected effective optical path
length exceeds the corresponding no-plasma reference path.

sources.leaf_definition: Optical path length variation due to the plasma
sources.parent_definition: Set of channels (lines-of-sight)

NAMES.name: line_integrated_electron_number_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Free-electron column density accumulated along a complete electromagnetic
propagation path, including both forward and return segments when present.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the column density of free electrons encountered along a
specified electromagnetic propagation path. It represents the total
free-electron content accumulated along the path, rather than the local
electron population at a point.

For the complete propagation path, the line-integrated electron density is
defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \int_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}} n_e(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-integrated electron density,
$n_e(\ell)$ is the local free-electron number density at path position
$\ell$, $\ell$ is arclength along the path, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}$ is
the complete propagation path.

The integral applies to the free-electron population along the full line of
sight and aggregates the local number density over arclength. For a
reflected propagation channel, the path includes both forward and return
segments, with no factor-of-two correction. The quantity excludes neutral or
bound electrons and is distinct from the local [electron
density](name:electron_density) and from a path average.

For a path with total arclength $L$, this quantity relates to the
[line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density)
through $N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = L\bar{n}_e$, where $L$ is the total path
arclength and $\bar{n}_e$ is the path-averaged free-electron number density.

NAMES.name: opacity_at_ece_channel_emission_position
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless optical depth along the electron-cyclotron-emission viewing
path at a channel emission position, indicating whether the detected
emission is local and thermal.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the optical depth of the plasma evaluated at the emission
position associated with one electron-cyclotron-emission channel. It
measures the cumulative attenuation between the emitting region and the
relevant observation path.

The optical depth is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{ECE}}(s_{\mathrm{em}}) = \int_{\mathcal{P}(s_{\mathrm{em}})} \alpha_{\mathrm{ECE}}(s)\,ds
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-emission optical
depth, $s_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the channel emission position,
$\mathcal{P}(s_{\mathrm{em}})$ is the line-of-sight path used to accumulate
the optical depth at that position, $\alpha_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the
electron-cyclotron-emission absorption coefficient, and $s$ is distance
along that path.

The scope is one channel and its associated emission position; values are
not summed or averaged over channels or over emission positions. This
quantity is the accumulated optical depth, not the local absorption
coefficient or a channel-integrated aggregate. It is the position-specific
form of [opacity](name:opacity), with the evaluation locus made explicit.

Optical depth greater than one indicates optically thick, locally thermal
emission, whereas optical depth less than one indicates that non-local or
suprathermal contributions can be important.

sources.leaf_definition: Optical depth of the plasma at the position of the measurement. This parameter is a proxy for the local / non-local character of the ECE emission. It must be greater than 1 to guarantee that the measurement is dominated by local ECE emission (non-local otherwise)
sources.parent_definition: Set of channels (frequency)

NAMES.name: poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position
NAMES.short:
Geometric poloidal angle locating a measurement position around the magnetic
axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) cross-section, increasing
clockwise.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal angle of a measurement position is the geometric angular
coordinate of a physical point about the magnetic axis in the poloidal
cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It
identifies the point's position around the magnetic axis, rather than a
field-line or toroidal angle.

Taking zero on the outward radial direction from the magnetic axis, the
angle is defined by

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{meas}} = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-\left(Z_{\mathrm{meas}}-Z_{\mathrm{axis}}\right),\,R_{\mathrm{meas}}-R_{\mathrm{axis}}\right]
$$

where $\theta_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the poloidal angle of the measurement
position, $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument arctangent that
preserves the angular quadrant, $R_{\mathrm{meas}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{meas}}$
are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of the measurement position,
and $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ are the corresponding
coordinates of the magnetic axis.

This quantity is evaluated pointwise at the designated measurement position
and is not a line average, flux-surface average, or signal-weighted
aggregate. It is the measurement-position specialization of
[poloidal_angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface), and it is distinct
from
[toroidal_angle_of_measurement_position](name:toroidal_angle_of_measurement_position),
which locates the same point around the symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short:
Signed equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function evaluated at a diagnostic
measurement location, identifying the nested magnetic surface intersecting
that location.
NAMES.long:
The signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ is the equilibrium flux function
evaluated at a physical measurement position. It labels the nested magnetic
surface passing through that position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the poloidal magnetic-flux function is
defined by

$$
\psi(R,Z) = \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\psi(R,Z)$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at cylindrical coordinates
$(R,Z)$, $B_Z(R',Z)$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, $R$ and $R'$
are major-radius coordinates, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\pi$ is the
circle constant. The toroidal angle $\phi$ completes the right-handed
cylindrical frame; axisymmetry makes $\psi$ independent of $\phi$.

This quantity applies to the equilibrium magnetic field at one physical
measurement position and has no species or population restriction. It is a
point evaluation, not a sum, average, or integral over multiple measurement
positions. It is not a normalized flux coordinate and does not represent a
perturbation or fluctuation of the equilibrium flux.

The same flux-function definition is used for [poloidal magnetic flux at a
beam-tracing point](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_beam_tracing_point), but
that quantity differs in evaluation locus. A normalized surface label at the
same type of location is [normalized poloidal flux coordinate at a
measurement position], which is derived by applying axis and boundary
references to the signed flux value.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net vertical magnetic flux through the
defining horizontal disk is directed in the $+Z$ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel
NAMES.short:
Equivalent blackbody temperature of electron cyclotron emission intensity
detected by a frequency-selective ECE channel, representing the radiation
brightness temperature.
NAMES.long:
Radiative temperature at an ECE channel is the equivalent blackbody
temperature associated with the detected electron cyclotron emission
intensity at that channel's selected frequency. It is a
brightness-temperature representation of the radiation, not the kinetic
temperature of the electron population.

For specific intensity represented by a blackbody spectrum, the radiation
temperature $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is defined by

$$
I_\nu = \frac{2h\nu^3}{c^2}\left[\exp\left(\frac{h\nu}{T_{\mathrm{rad}}}\right)-1\right]^{-1}
$$

where $I_\nu$ is the detected specific intensity at frequency $\nu$, $h$ is
Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the
energy-equivalent blackbody temperature.

The quantity applies to one ECE channel and its selected frequency; it is
not summed or averaged over channels. It excludes the separate kinetic
electron temperature and polarization-resolved radiation quantities. When
the emitting plasma is optically thick, $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ approaches the
local electron temperature. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) uses the same
brightness-temperature definition at a different evaluation locus.

NAMES.name: spectral_calibration_factor_at_line_of_sight
NAMES.short:
Wavelength-specific interferometric conversion coefficient that converts a
signed phase change along a line of sight into electron column density.
NAMES.long:
The spectral calibration factor is the wavelength-specific proportionality
that maps an interferometric phase change along one line of sight to the
electron column density on that optical path.

The conversion is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = K_{\mathrm{spec}}\,\Delta\varphi
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the [line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density), $K_{\mathrm{spec}}$
is this spectral calibration factor, and $\Delta\varphi$ is the signed
interferometric phase change.

The factor applies to the complete electron-density integral along the
associated line of sight and to its corresponding probing wavelength. It
represents the electron contribution only and is not a local density, a
line-averaged density, or an optical phase itself.

Applying this factor produces the line-integrated electron number density;
dividing that result by the optical chord length gives [line-averaged
electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density). The associated
wavelength is the spectral parameter of the probing electromagnetic wave,
related to [wavelength of wave beam](name:wavelength_of_wave_beam).

sources.leaf_definition: Conversion factor to be used to convert phase into line density for this wavelength
sources.parent_definition: Set of wavelengths used for interferometry

NAMES.name: total_electron_count
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Total inventory of free electrons within the plasma, including thermal and
fast populations and excluding electrons bound in atoms or molecules.
NAMES.long:
The total free-electron count is the number of unbound electrons contained
within the plasma volume, aggregated over all electron populations.

$$
N_e = \int_V n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $N_e$ is the total free-electron count, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
[total electron density](name:total_electron_density), $\mathbf{x}$ is
position, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $V$ is the plasma
volume.

This quantity includes thermal, fast, and other free-electron populations
present within $V$ and sums them over the entire plasma volume. It excludes
electrons bound in neutral atoms or molecules and is distinct from local or
volume-averaged density, which describes electrons per physical volume
rather than the integrated inventory.

The count is obtained by integrating the complete local electron density; a
[line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density)
represents a chord average and cannot substitute for this volume integral.

sources.leaf_definition: Total number of electrons in the plasma, estimated from the line densities measured by the various channels

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_ece_channel
NAMES.short:
Signed vertical coordinate of an electron-cyclotron-emission channel’s
measurement position in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate of an electron-cyclotron-emission (ECE) channel is
the signed projection of its measurement position onto the vertical
direction.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{ECE}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ECE}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the vertical coordinate,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the position vector of the channel’s
measurement location, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the measurement position associated with one ECE
channel and is not averaged or summed over channels. It describes the
channel position rather than an ECE signal, frequency, or plasma-field
value.

It is distinct from the radial coordinate $R$ and toroidal angle $\phi$. The
[vertical coordinate of a measurement
position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position) expresses the
same geometric quantity for a generic measurement location, whereas this
entry retains the ECE-channel locus.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the ECE channel measurement position lies in
the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_line_of_sight
NAMES.short:
Signed vertical coordinate of a designated point defining a diagnostic line
of sight in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate of a designated point defining a diagnostic line of
sight specifies that point's height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height.

This quantity applies to one geometric point used to define the line of
sight, including the designated first point of the sight-line geometry. It
is a point coordinate, not an average, integral, or quantity accumulated
along the line of sight.

It does not represent the line-of-sight direction, optical path length, or
any plasma quantity evaluated along the sight line. Its geometric role is
analogous to the [vertical coordinate of a
camera](name:vertical_coordinate_of_camera) and the [vertical coordinate of
an aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture), which locate other
diagnostic components.

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short:
Fringe-jump-corrected phase angle of a probing electromagnetic signal at a
selected wavelength, referenced to the channel’s defined launch phase.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the continuous phase angle of a probing electromagnetic
signal at one selected wavelength, with integer-cycle discontinuities caused
by fringe jumps removed. It represents the phase accumulated along the
signal’s propagation chord relative to the channel’s defined launch-phase
reference.

The corrected phase is related to the measured wrapped phase by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{corr}} = \phi_{\mathrm{meas}} + 2\pi N_{\mathrm{fj}}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the fringe-jump-corrected phase,
$\phi_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the measured wrapped phase, and $N_{\mathrm{fj}}$
is the signed integer number of full-cycle fringe-jump corrections. The
factor $2\pi$ represents one complete phase revolution.

The quantity applies to a single probing wavelength and represents the phase
accumulated over the complete propagation chord, rather than a local phase
at one point. It is referenced to the channel’s defined launch phase; it is
not an absolute electromagnetic phase and does not include an uncorrected
fringe discontinuity.

The corrected phase is the phase observable used to obtain the
[line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) through the
wavelength-dependent plasma refractive index. It is distinct from the
general [reference phase](name:reference_phase), which establishes a phase
origin without specifying fringe-jump correction or a propagation chord.

NAMES.name: wavelength_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short:
Vacuum spatial period of a probing electromagnetic wave propagating as a
diagnostic beam, defining its spectral wavelength.
NAMES.long:
Vacuum wavelength of a wave beam is the spatial period of its
electromagnetic phase in vacuum, assigned to the beam’s carrier radiation.
It characterizes the beam itself rather than a spectral transition or an
instrument-response feature.

The vacuum wavelength $\lambda_0$ is related to the beam’s temporal
frequency $f$ by:

$$
\lambda_0 = \frac{c}{f}
$$

where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum and $f$ is the temporal
oscillation frequency of the electromagnetic wave.

This quantity applies to a probing electromagnetic wave beam and describes
its vacuum propagation property, independent of plasma-induced changes in
phase velocity. It is assigned to the beam as a whole and is not a sum,
average, or integral over beams, paths, channels, or spectral components. It
excludes the in-medium wavelength and wavelengths associated with filters,
detector pixels, or spectral transitions.

This beam-specific specialization of [vacuum electromagnetic wavelength]
supplies the wavelength used to characterize the beam’s propagation and its
interaction with plasma. For a vacuum plane wave, the magnitude of its [wave
vector] satisfies the equivalent relation $|\mathbf{k}| = 2\pi/\lambda_0$,
where $\mathbf{k}$ is the vacuum wave vector.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged along a
complete plasma propagation chord, equal to the path integral divided by
chord length.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged along a
complete propagation chord is the path-normalized continuum count density of
the unqualified free-electron population along that chord.

For local [electron density](name:electron_density) $n_e(l)$, the defining
relation is:

$$
\bar{n}_e = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_e(l)\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_e$ is the line-averaged electron density, $n_e(l)$ is the
local free-electron density at path coordinate $l$, $l$ is distance along
the complete propagation chord, and $L$ is the full chord length.

This quantity applies to the complete unqualified free-electron population
along the chord, aggregating all contributing free-electron populations
rather than selecting thermal or fast electrons. It is a path average over
the chord and is not a pointwise [electron density](name:electron_density)
or a line-integrated column density.

The numerator in the defining relation is the [line-integrated electron
number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density); dividing it
by the chord length produces this path-normalized quantity. The same
line-averaging construction applies to species-specific quantities such as
[line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while
this quantity remains specific to free electrons.

NAMES.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless normalized toroidal-flux label that maps a physical
measurement position onto a nested magnetic surface between the magnetic
axis and equilibrium boundary.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the dimensionless normalized toroidal-flux coordinate
evaluated at a physical measurement position. It maps that position to the
nested magnetic surface passing through it, rather than representing a
cylindrical distance or local vector component.

For a measurement position, the coordinate is defined from the toroidal
magnetic flux labeling the surface through that position:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_m) = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_m)-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_m)$ is the normalized
toroidal-flux coordinate at measurement position $\mathbf{x}_m$,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathbf{x}_m)$ is the toroidal magnetic flux labeling
the magnetic surface through that position, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is
its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its
value at the equilibrium boundary.

The evaluation locus is the physical measurement position. This is a point
value of the equilibrium coordinate, with no averaging, summation, or
integration over a channel, path, region, or population; within the
normalized domain, the magnetic axis corresponds to zero and the boundary
reference corresponds to one.

It is the position-specific specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), retaining the same
magnetic-surface label while evaluating it at $\mathbf{x}_m$. It is distinct
from the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma
boundary](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary),
which supplies the outer normalization reference rather than the coordinate
of an arbitrary measurement position.

NAMES.name: radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short:
Temperature-equivalent radiation energy scale of electron-cyclotron
emission, evaluated at the magnetic axis, the degenerate innermost magnetic
surface where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes. It is a
brightness-temperature quantity, not necessarily the local kinetic electron
temperature.
NAMES.long:
Temperature-equivalent radiation energy scale of electron-cyclotron
emission, evaluated at the magnetic axis. The magnetic axis is the
degenerate innermost magnetic surface of the equilibrium, the locus in the
poloidal cross-section where the gradient of the [poloidal magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes; evaluation at this locus does
not imply that the radiative temperature has an extremum there.

The blackbody-equivalent radiation energy scale is defined by matching the
radiation field's specific intensity to the Planck spectral intensity:

$$
I_\nu = \frac{2 h \nu^3}{c^2}\left[\exp\!\left(\frac{h\nu}{T_\mathrm{rad}}\right)-1\right]^{-1}
$$

where $I_\nu$ is the radiation specific intensity, $\nu$ is the radiation
frequency, $h$ is the Planck constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and
$T_\mathrm{rad}$ is the [radiative temperature].

This quantity is restricted to the radiation field associated with
electron-cyclotron emission at the magnetic-axis locus. For layer-resolved
electron-cyclotron emission, the axis value is the radiative temperature of
the resonance layer whose effective emission location is closest to the
magnetic axis; the aggregation convention is nearest-layer selection, not a
spatial average over neighboring layers. Ordinary-mode and
extraordinary-mode electron-cyclotron emission are polarization-specific
variants; the unqualified quantity does not select a polarization mode and
is not a sum or mean over modes.

It is the radiation-field member of [temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:temperature_at_magnetic_axis) and the magnetic-axis counterpart
of [radiative temperature]. It must not be identified with the local kinetic
[electron temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) except in the limiting
case of optically thick thermal emission, where the brightness temperature
approaches the electron thermal energy scale.

NAMES.name: current_of_poloidal_field_coil
NAMES.short:
Conventional electrical current through a poloidal-field coil winding, with
sign set by winding orientation and distinct from the winding’s ampere-turn
product.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the conventional current carried by the conductor forming a
poloidal-field coil winding. It describes the circuit current itself,
independent of the number of turns in the winding, and is the
poloidal-field-coil counterpart of [current of a toroidal-field
coil](name:current_of_toroidal_field_coil).

The current is defined by the rate of conventional charge flow:

$$
I = \frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

where $I$ is the winding current, $Q$ is the net transported electric
charge, and $t$ is time. For a winding with $N$ series-connected turns, its
magnetomotive effect is proportional to the ampere-turn product $NI$; $N$ is
the dimensionless number of turns. This quantity is not the coil resistance
or the resulting voltage drop, which is related to [poloidal-field-coil
resistance](name:resistance_of_poloidal_field_coil).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional current follows the positive
reference direction assigned around the poloidal-field-coil winding.

sources.leaf_definition: Current fed in the coil (for 1 turn, to be multiplied by the number of turns to obtain the generated magnetic field), positive when the current is counter-clockwise when seen from above.
sources.parent_definition: Active PF coils

NAMES.name: derivative_of_area_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate
NAMES.short:
Radial rate of change of the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed by a
nested magnetic flux surface as the toroidal flux coordinate increases.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local derivative of the poloidal cross-sectional area
enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its dimensionful
toroidal flux coordinate. It describes how the enclosed cross section
changes along the equilibrium’s radial flux labeling.

$$
\frac{dA(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}})}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
$$

where $A(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}})$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed
by the magnetic flux surface labeled by $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, and
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate.

The quantity applies locally to each nested closed magnetic flux surface and
uses no population or species aggregation. It is a differential rate, not
the cross-sectional area itself, and it does not denote the total
three-dimensional area of the toroidal surface or the enclosed plasma
volume. It is the derivative specialization of area_of_flux_surface. The
related
[derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate)
uses the same flux coordinate but differentiates enclosed volume rather than
poloidal cross-sectional area.

sources.leaf_definition: Radial derivative of the cross-sectional area of the flux surface with respect to rho_tor
sources.parent_definition: Equilibrium profiles (1D radial grid) as a function of the poloidal flux

NAMES.name: elongation_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short:
Ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axes of a nested magnetic flux
surface’s poloidal cross-section, independent of its overall size.
NAMES.long:
Elongation is the shape ratio of an individual nested magnetic flux surface,
describing how extended its poloidal cross-section is vertically relative to
horizontally.

For a given flux surface, the elongation is defined by

$$
\kappa = \frac{a_v}{a_h}
$$

where $\kappa$ is the elongation, $a_v$ is the vertical semi-axis of the
poloidal cross-section, and $a_h$ is its horizontal semi-axis.

The quantity applies separately to each nested magnetic flux surface and is
a shape ratio rather than an integrated, summed, or averaged quantity. It is
not restricted to the outermost surface; the distinct [elongation of the
plasma boundary](name:elongation_of_plasma_boundary) refers specifically to
the last closed plasma boundary.

The [radial derivative of elongation of a flux surface] describes the change
of $\kappa$ across nested surfaces, whereas this quantity gives the
elongation at one surface.

NAMES.name: elongation_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio of the plasma boundary’s vertical half-height to its
minor radius, quantifying the elongation of its cross-sectional shape.
NAMES.long:
Plasma-boundary elongation is the ratio of the vertical half-height to the
minor radius of the outermost closed plasma cross-section, describing its
vertical shaping relative to a circular cross-section.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the elongation
is defined by

$$
\kappa = \frac{Z_{\max}-Z_{\min}}{2a}
$$

where $\kappa$ is the plasma-boundary elongation, $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$
are the maximum and minimum vertical coordinates of the boundary, and $a$ is
the minor radius, defined as the radial half-width of the boundary
cross-section.

This quantity applies specifically to the plasma boundary rather than to an
arbitrary nested magnetic flux surface. Its geometric aggregation uses the
full vertical extent and radial half-width of the boundary cross-section; it
is not a local field value and is not averaged over the boundary. It
therefore excludes the corresponding elongation of an interior flux surface.

The quantity is the boundary-locus specialization of [elongation of a flux
surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface), which applies the same geometric
ratio to a general nested magnetic flux-surface cross-section.
